title: Engagement endpoint tests omit cross-scope authorization cases
reasoning: The endpoint tests verify authentication, missing IDs, invalid IDs, and that two users can track the same devotional, but they do not cover whether an authenticated user may submit a valid devotional/prayer/fast ID outside their church or otherwise outside their allowed scope. If these endpoints accept any existing object ID, analytics events can be created for resources the user should not be associated with, polluting engagement data and potentially exposing object existence through response behavior.
recommendation: Add negative authorization tests with a second church and resources not associated with the authenticated user's profile. Assert the endpoint returns 403 or 400 and creates no event, matching the intended API contract.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests only distinguish valid object IDs from nonexistent or nonnumeric IDs, and the multi-user case uses the same devotional rather than an out-of-scope resource.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create church_b, fast_b/day_b/devotional_b/prayer_set_b, authenticate a user from church_a, POST those valid IDs to each tracking endpoint, and assert no Event is created.
minimumFixScope: Add cross-church/out-of-scope cases for each ID-based engagement tracking endpoint.
